rules.statement: Don't read `HttpContext` or `IHttpContextAccessor` from code that runs in an interactive Blazor Server component or circuit. Get the user from the circuit's authentication state or from a connection-scoped session instead.
rules.why: Microsoft documents `IHttpContextAccessor` as unavailable in interactive components, and the hub's response has already started by the time a component runs.
rules.check: Look for `IHttpContextAccessor` injected into, or `HttpContext` used by, Razor components, circuit handlers or services that run per circuit.

rules.statement: Define each name that crosses between a server and its browser client once, in a package with no project or framework references that both sides reference. This covers JSON property names, persisted-state keys, claim types, endpoint paths and header defaults. Never keep a copy in the client.
rules.why: A wire contract that exists in two copies drifts, and a name that differs by one character fails only in a browser.
rules.check: Look for string constants in a WebAssembly client that duplicate server-side names, and for shared names added to a package the browser client cannot reference.

rules.statement: A package that runs in the browser (Blazor WebAssembly) must not reference the ASP.NET Core shared framework, or any package that needs it.
rules.why: The ASP.NET Core shared framework does not run in the browser.
rules.check: Look in browser client .csproj files for a `FrameworkReference` to Microsoft.AspNetCore.App, or a project or package reference to a server-side abstractions or implementation package.

rules.statement: An implementation package references only abstractions packages, never a sibling implementation package. Put a contract that two implementations share into an abstractions package or a dependency-free package.
rules.why: An implementation package that references a sibling implementation package gives up the rule that keeps each package replaceable.
rules.check: Look in an implementation package's .csproj for a ProjectReference or PackageReference to another implementation (non-Abstractions) package of the same family.

rules.statement: When you add or change a package whose references form a boundary, such as a browser-run client, add or update a dependency test that checks its assembly references. For a browser client, the test is an allow-list.
rules.why: A stray reference should fail its dependency test rather than fail in a browser.
rules.check: Look for a new browser-run or dependency-free package, or a changed reference, that has no matching dependency test, or whose test uses a deny-list where an allow-list is needed.

rules.statement: Never send an access or refresh token to a Blazor WebAssembly or other browser-run client. A user document or persisted state sent to the browser carries only the configured user claims, the logout URL and its guard.
rules.why: A component that runs in the browser exposes any token to injected script (RFC 10017).
rules.check: Look for tokens added to persisted component state, to the user endpoint's response, or to any DTO the WebAssembly client receives.

rules.statement: Don't rely on a custom anti-forgery header to guard a SignalR hub or WebSocket endpoint. Refuse the upgrade when Fetch Metadata shows a cross-site request, or when the `Origin` is neither the frontend's public origin nor a trusted origin.
rules.why: A browser `WebSocket` cannot send a custom header, so the header check cannot protect a hub.
rules.check: Look at hub endpoint guards that require the anti-forgery header, or that skip the Fetch Metadata and Origin checks.

rules.statement: A request to a hub must not write a cookie to the upgraded response. It slides the session and obtains tokens through the connection's session, which holds the session handle in memory for the life of the connection.
rules.why: The response of an upgraded hub request has already started, and the connection has no `HttpContext` after it opens.
rules.check: Look for session refresh or `Set-Cookie` writes on code paths that handle hub or WebSocket requests.

rules.statement: Issue a token only to the request of a guarded endpoint, or to a connection that a guarded hub request opened.
rules.why: Tokens must not leak to unguarded endpoints or to connections that no guarded request authenticated.
rules.check: Look for token accessors or handlers that can run for unguarded endpoints, or for connections that lack the guarded connection session.

rules.statement: Session revalidation for a long-lived connection or circuit fails closed. Sign the user out on any revalidation error except an unavailable store, and keep the revalidation interval at most half the session's idle timeout.
rules.why: A circuit must not stay signed in after its session has ended or cannot be verified, while a store outage alone should not sign every user out.
rules.check: Look at revalidation catch blocks that keep the user signed in on unexpected errors, and at options validation that lets the revalidation interval exceed half the idle timeout.

rules.statement: Reserve the claim types the BFF itself puts on the session principal, such as the logout action and guard, and drop them from the claims the identity provider returns.
rules.why: A provider-supplied claim with a reserved type could spoof the logout form's action or guard.
rules.check: Look for new internal claim types added to the session principal without being filtered out of incoming provider claims.
